name: Red Lentil Soup
description: A classic, creamy Turkish soup made with red lentils.
steps: Dice the onion, carrot, and potato into small cubes.
Sauté the vegetables in butter, then stir in the flour.
Add the lentils and 1.5 litres of water, and simmer for 25 minutes until the vegetables are soft.
Blend until smooth, season with cumin and salt, and serve hot.

name: Ezogelin Soup
description: A spiced soup of red lentils, rice, and bulgur.
steps: Sauté the onion in butter and stir in the tomato paste.
Add the lentils, rice, bulgur, and water, and stir to combine.
Simmer over low heat for 30 minutes until everything is tender.
Season with mint, chili flakes, and salt, then serve.

name: Imam Bayildi
description: Aubergines stuffed with a sweet onion filling and slow-cooked in olive oil.
steps: Peel the aubergines and fry or roast until soft.
Sauté the onion, garlic, and tomato in olive oil to make the filling.
Split the aubergines open and stuff with the filling.
Drizzle with water and olive oil, then bake for 25 minutes and serve cold.

name: Karniyarik (Split-Belly Aubergine)
description: Aubergines stuffed with a minced meat filling and baked in the oven.
steps: Peel the aubergines, fry them, then slit them open lengthwise.
Brown the minced meat with onion and garlic, then add tomato and seasoning.
Fill the aubergines with the mixture and top with tomato and pepper slices.
Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 25 minutes.

name: Turkish Manti (Dumplings)
description: Tiny meat-filled dumplings served with garlicky yoghurt and melted butter.
steps: Knead a firm dough from flour, egg, salt, and water, then let it rest.
Mix the minced meat and onion to make the filling.
Roll the dough thin, cut into small squares, fill, and pinch closed.
Boil until cooked, then serve with garlicky yoghurt and melted butter sauce.

name: Olive Oil Stuffed Vine Leaves
description: Vine leaves rolled around a rice and herb filling.
steps: Sauté the onion in olive oil, then add the rice, currants, and pine nuts.
Season the filling with herbs and spices and cook briefly.
Place a small amount of filling on each leaf and roll up tightly.
Arrange in a pot and simmer with water and lemon juice for 35 minutes over low heat.

name: Menemen (Turkish Scrambled Eggs)
description: A quick Turkish breakfast of eggs cooked with tomato and pepper.
steps: Sauté the peppers in olive oil.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook until the liquid reduces.
Crack in the eggs and cook, stirring gently or leaving them softly set.
Season with salt and chili flakes and serve hot.

name: Izmir-Style Meatballs
description: Baked meatballs with potatoes in a tomato sauce.
steps: Knead the minced meat with onion, garlic, bread, and egg, then shape into meatballs.
Lightly fry the meatballs.
Slice the potatoes and arrange in a baking dish, then place the meatballs on top.
Add tomato and pepper, and bake at 180°C (350°F) for 30 minutes.

name: Kisir (Bulgur Salad)
description: A refreshing salad of fine bulgur, tomato paste, and fresh herbs.
steps: Soak the bulgur in hot water and stir in the tomato and pepper pastes.
Once the bulgur has softened, add the chopped vegetables and herbs.
Toss with lemon juice, pomegranate molasses, and olive oil.
Chill in the fridge and serve cold.

name: Smoky Aubergine Salad
description: A traditional meze of smoky charred aubergine and yoghurt.
steps: Char-grill the aubergines and peel off the skins.
Chop the flesh and mix with crushed garlic and yoghurt.
Season with lemon juice and salt.
Drizzle with olive oil and serve cold.

name: Shepherd's Salad
description: A classic finely diced salad of tomato, cucumber, and pepper.
steps: Dice all the vegetables into small cubes.
Finely chop the parsley and add it in.
Toss with olive oil, lemon juice, and salt.
Transfer to a serving dish and serve right away.

name: Turlu (Mixed Vegetable Stew)
description: A hearty stew of seasonal vegetables cooked together in olive oil.
steps: Cut all the vegetables into large chunks.
Sauté the onion and garlic in olive oil.
Add the remaining vegetables and toss for a few minutes.
Add the tomato and water, then simmer over low heat for 35 minutes.

name: Horiatiki (Greek Salad)
description: The classic Greek salad with feta cheese and olives.
steps: Roughly chop the tomato, cucumber, pepper, and onion.
Add the olives and a block of feta cheese.
Season with olive oil and oregano.
Add salt just before serving.

name: Moussaka
description: Layers of aubergine, spiced minced meat, and creamy béchamel, baked until golden.
steps: Slice the aubergine and potato and lightly fry.
Brown the minced meat with onion and tomato to make the sauce.
Make a béchamel sauce from butter, flour, and milk.
Layer the vegetables, meat sauce, and béchamel, then bake for 35 minutes.

name: Tzatziki
description: A cooling dip of strained yoghurt, cucumber, and garlic.
steps: Grate the cucumber and squeeze out the excess water.
Mix the yoghurt with crushed garlic and the cucumber.
Season with dill and salt.
Drizzle with olive oil and serve cold.

name: Spanakopita (Spinach Pie)
description: Layered filo pastry filled with spinach and feta cheese.
steps: Sauté the spinach with onion, then drain off any liquid.
Mix in the feta cheese, egg, and dill to make the filling.
Layer the filo sheets brushed with melted butter and the filling.
Bake at 180°C (350°F) until golden brown.

name: Chicken Souvlaki
description: Marinated chicken skewers, grilled and served with warm pita.
steps: Cube the chicken and marinate with olive oil, lemon, garlic, and oregano.
Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Thread onto skewers and grill or pan-fry.
Serve hot with warm pita bread.

name: Fasolada (Greek Bean Soup)
description: Greece's national soup, simmered with dried beans.
steps: Soak the dried beans overnight.
Sauté the vegetables in olive oil and stir in the tomato paste.
Add the beans and water and simmer until tender.
Season with salt and serve hot.

name: Gemista (Stuffed Tomatoes and Peppers)
description: Tomatoes and peppers baked with a rice and herb filling.
steps: Hollow out the tomatoes and peppers, reserving the flesh.
Mix the rice, onion, and herbs to make the filling.
Stuff the vegetables with the filling and arrange in a baking dish.
Drizzle with olive oil and bake for 40 minutes.

name: Pastitsio
description: A Greek baked pasta dish with minced meat sauce and béchamel.
steps: Boil the pasta until al dente.
Brown the minced meat with onion and tomato to make the sauce.
Make a béchamel sauce from butter, flour, and milk.
Layer the pasta, meat sauce, and béchamel, then bake.

name: Fava (Yellow Split Pea Purée)
description: A silky-smooth Greek meze made from yellow split peas.
steps: Simmer the split peas with onion until soft.
Blend until smooth.
Stir in the olive oil and lemon juice.
Serve warm or chilled.

name: Caprese Salad
description: A simple Italian salad of tomato, mozzarella, and basil.
steps: Slice the tomato and mozzarella.
Arrange the tomato, mozzarella, and basil leaves alternately on a plate.
Drizzle with olive oil and balsamic vinegar.
Sprinkle with salt and serve immediately.

name: Minestrone
description: A hearty Italian soup of seasonal vegetables and pasta.
steps: Sauté the onion, carrot, and celery in olive oil.
Add the tomato and beans with water and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the courgette and pasta and cook until the pasta is done.
Season with salt and serve hot.

name: Bruschetta
description: Toasted bread topped with tomato and basil.
steps: Slice and toast the bread, then rub with garlic.
Dice the tomatoes and mix with basil.
Season with olive oil and salt.
Spoon the mixture over the toasted bread slices and serve.

name: Panzanella (Tuscan Bread Salad)
description: A Tuscan-style salad of stale bread and tomato.
steps: Cube the stale bread and lightly toast it.
Chop the tomato, cucumber, and onion.
Combine everything and add the basil.
Toss with olive oil, vinegar, and salt, then rest for 10 minutes.

name: Pasta alla Norma
description: A Sicilian pasta with aubergine and tomato sauce.
steps: Cube the aubergine and fry in olive oil.
Make a sauce with garlic and tomato, then add the aubergine.
Boil the pasta and toss with the sauce.
Top with cheese and basil, then serve.

name: Mushroom Risotto
description: A creamy Italian risotto of arborio rice and mushrooms.
steps: Sauté the mushrooms in butter and set aside.
Sauté the onion, then add the rice and stir until translucent.
Add the wine and hot stock gradually, stirring constantly.
Once the rice is cooked, stir in the mushrooms, butter, and parmesan.

name: Caponata
description: A sweet-and-sour Sicilian relish of aubergine, celery, and olives.
steps: Cube the aubergine and fry in olive oil.
Sauté the celery and onion separately.
Add the tomato, olives, and capers, and cook together.
Stir in the vinegar and cook for 5 more minutes, then serve cold.

name: Aglio e Olio
description: A simple Italian spaghetti with garlic and olive oil.
steps: Boil the spaghetti in salted water.
Gently cook the garlic in olive oil over low heat until lightly golden.
Add the chili flakes and toss with the cooked pasta.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve hot.

name: Margherita Pizza
description: The classic Italian pizza with tomato sauce, mozzarella, and basil.
steps: Roll out the dough and spread with tomato sauce.
Scatter over the sliced mozzarella.
Bake in a preheated oven at high heat for 10 minutes.
Top with basil and a drizzle of olive oil, then serve.

name: Gazpacho
description: A chilled Spanish soup made from raw vegetables.
steps: Roughly chop all the vegetables.
Blend the vegetables with garlic, vinegar, and olive oil.
Season with salt and chill in the fridge for at least 1 hour.
Serve cold.

name: Paella
description: Spain's famous saffron rice with chicken and seafood.
steps: Brown the chicken in olive oil and set aside.
Sauté the onion and tomato, then add the rice.
Add the hot saffron-infused stock and return the chicken to the pan.
In the final 10 minutes, add the prawns and mussels and continue cooking.

name: Patatas Bravas
description: Crispy fried potatoes with a spicy tomato sauce, a Spanish tapas classic.
steps: Cube the potatoes and fry or roast until crisp.
Make a sauce with garlic, tomato paste, and chili flakes.
Toss the fried potatoes with the sauce.
Serve hot.

name: Tortilla Española
description: A Spanish-style omelette made with potato and egg.
steps: Thinly slice the potato and onion and cook gently in plenty of olive oil until soft.
Beat the eggs and mix in the potatoes.
Cook in a pan, flipping to brown both sides.
Slice and serve warm.

name: Salmorejo
description: A thick, chilled Andalusian soup of tomato and bread.
steps: Roughly chop the tomatoes and blend with the bread.
Add the garlic, vinegar, and salt and blend again.
Slowly drizzle in the olive oil while blending until smooth.
Chill for at least 1 hour and serve cold.

name: Pisto
description: A Spanish-style vegetable medley of courgette, aubergine, and pepper.
steps: Cube all the vegetables.
Sauté the onion and pepper in olive oil.
Add the aubergine, courgette, and tomato, and cook over low heat.
Once the vegetables are soft, season with salt and serve.

name: Tabbouleh
description: A Levantine salad packed with fresh parsley and fine bulgur.
steps: Soak the bulgur in a little water and let it soften.
Finely chop the parsley, mint, tomato, and spring onion.
Combine the bulgur with the chopped ingredients.
Toss with lemon juice, olive oil, and salt, then serve.

name: Fattoush
description: A crisp Levantine salad topped with toasted pita.
steps: Break the pita into pieces and toast or fry until crisp.
Chop the vegetables and combine in a large bowl.
Make a dressing with pomegranate molasses, olive oil, sumac, and salt.
Toss in the toasted pita just before serving.

name: Baba Ganoush
description: A smoky Levantine dip of charred aubergine and tahini.
steps: Char the aubergines over a flame or in the oven.
Peel and mash the flesh.
Mix with tahini, lemon juice, and crushed garlic.
Drizzle with olive oil and serve.

name: Falafel
description: A Levantine classic of fried spiced chickpea patties.
steps: Soak the chickpeas overnight; do not boil before use.
Process the chickpeas, onion, garlic, parsley, and spices in a food processor.
Shape the mixture into small patties.
Deep-fry in hot oil until golden brown.

name: Shakshuka
description: Eggs poached in a spiced tomato sauce.
steps: Sauté the onion, pepper, and garlic in olive oil.
Add the tomato and cumin and simmer until a thick sauce forms.
Make wells in the sauce and crack in the eggs.
Cover and cook until the whites are set but the yolks are still soft.

name: Muhammara
description: A sweet-and-spicy Levantine dip of roasted red pepper and walnuts.
steps: Char-grill the red peppers and peel off the skins.
Process the peppers, walnuts, breadcrumbs, and pomegranate molasses together.
Stir in the chili flakes and salt.
Drizzle with olive oil and serve.

name: Hummus
description: A creamy Levantine dip of chickpeas and tahini.
steps: Blend the cooked chickpeas with their cooking liquid until smooth.
Add the tahini, lemon juice, and garlic, and blend again until creamy.
Season with cumin and salt.
Drizzle with olive oil and serve.

name: Manakish
description: Levantine flatbread topped with za'atar and olive oil.
steps: Knead the flour, yeast, salt, and water into a dough and let it rise for 1 hour.
Divide the dough into rounds and flatten them out.
Spread with the thyme and olive oil mixture.
Bake in a preheated oven for 10-12 minutes.

name: Warak Enab (Levantine Stuffed Vine Leaves)
description: Vine leaves rolled around a rice and herb filling, Levantine style.
steps: Mix the rice with chopped tomato and herbs to make the filling.
Place a small amount of filling on each leaf and roll up tightly.
Arrange the rolls snugly in a pot.
Add water, lemon juice, and olive oil, then simmer over low heat for 35 minutes.

name: Chicken Tagine
description: A sweet-and-savoury Moroccan chicken dish with apricots and almonds.
steps: Sear the chicken in olive oil.
Add the onion and spices and sauté for a few minutes.
Add the apricots and a little water, cover, and cook for 35 minutes.
Scatter with toasted almonds and serve.

name: Couscous Salad
description: A light and refreshing Moroccan couscous salad.
steps: Pour hot water over the couscous, let it stand, then fluff with a fork.
Dice the cucumber and tomato.
Combine the couscous with the vegetables and chopped mint.
Season with lemon juice, olive oil, and salt, then serve.

name: Harira Soup
description: A spiced Moroccan soup of lentils and chickpeas.
steps: Sauté the onion and celery in olive oil.
Add the tomato, lentils, chickpeas, and spices, then pour in water.
Simmer over low heat for 30 minutes.
Whisk the flour with a little water and stir in to thicken, then serve.

name: Zaalouk
description: A spiced Moroccan relish of aubergine and tomato.
steps: Cube the aubergine and boil or roast until soft.
Cook with tomato and garlic in olive oil.
Mash the aubergine in as you stir.
Season with cumin, chili flakes, and salt, then serve cold.

name: Moroccan Carrot Salad
description: Boiled carrot salad seasoned with cumin and cinnamon.
steps: Slice the carrots and boil until tender.
Toss with lemon juice, cumin, and cinnamon.
Add the olive oil and chopped parsley.
Serve warm or chilled.

name: Ezme (Spicy Tomato & Pepper Salad)
description: A finely chopped, fiery Turkish tomato and pepper relish dressed with pomegranate molasses.
steps: Finely chop the tomatoes, green pepper, red onion, garlic, and parsley — as fine as you can manage.
Combine everything in a bowl with the pomegranate molasses, olive oil, and chilli flakes.
Season with salt and mix well, mashing slightly with a spoon so the juices release.
Rest for 10 minutes before serving with warm flatbread.

name: Haydari (Garlic Yoghurt Dip)
description: A thick, garlicky strained yoghurt dip finished with fresh mint and olive oil.
steps: Crush the garlic to a paste with a pinch of salt.
Stir the garlic, dried mint, and finely chopped dill through the yoghurt.
Spoon into a shallow bowl and drizzle generously with olive oil.
Chill for at least 30 minutes before serving with warm pide or flatbread.

name: Piyaz (White Bean Salad)
description: A tangy Turkish white bean salad with onion, tomato, and a lemony dressing.
steps: Drain and rinse the white beans and tip them into a large bowl.
Thinly slice the red onion and toss with the sumac to soften its bite.
Add the onion, diced tomato, and chopped parsley to the beans.
Dress with olive oil, lemon juice, and salt, then toss gently and serve at room temperature.

name: Sigara Böreği (Fried Cheese Pastry Rolls)
description: Crisp, cigar-shaped pastry rolls filled with feta and parsley.
steps: Mash the feta with the chopped parsley to make the filling.
Cut each yufka sheet into triangles, place a spoonful of filling at the wide end, and roll tightly into a cigar shape, sealing the tip with beaten egg.
Heat the sunflower oil in a pan over medium heat.
Fry the rolls in batches until golden and crisp on all sides, then drain on paper towels and serve hot.

name: Melitzanosalata (Greek Aubergine Dip)
description: A smoky, garlicky Greek aubergine dip brightened with lemon and olive oil.
steps: Char the aubergines whole over a flame or under a hot grill until the skin blisters and the flesh softens, about 20 minutes.
Let them cool, then peel away the skin and drain the flesh in a sieve for 10 minutes.
Finely chop the flesh and mix with crushed garlic, olive oil, lemon juice, and red wine vinegar.
Season with salt, stir through chopped parsley, and serve at room temperature.

name: Taramasalata
description: A pale, creamy Greek dip made from cured fish roe, bread, and olive oil.
steps: Soak the crustless white bread in water, then squeeze it as dry as possible.
Blend the bread with the tarama and grated onion until smooth.
With the blender running, drizzle in the olive oil a little at a time until the mixture is pale and creamy.
Stir in lemon juice to taste and chill before serving with crusty bread.

name: Saganaki (Fried Cheese)
description: Pan-fried cheese with a golden crust, finished with a squeeze of lemon.
steps: Slice the cheese into thick pieces and dust lightly with flour.
Heat the olive oil in a heavy pan until shimmering.
Fry the cheese for about 90 seconds per side until deeply golden.
Transfer to a plate and squeeze fresh lemon juice over the top just before serving.

name: Sambousek (Cheese-Filled Pastries)
description: Half-moon pastries filled with melted cheese and fried until golden and crisp.
steps: Combine the flour, olive oil, salt, and enough warm water to form a smooth dough; rest for 20 minutes.
Grate the halloumi, crumble the feta, and mix with chopped mint for the filling.
Roll the dough thin, cut into circles, and fold each with a spoonful of filling into a sealed half-moon.
Deep-fry in hot sunflower oil until golden on both sides, then drain and serve warm.

name: Labneh with Za'atar
description: Tangy strained yoghurt cheese, served pooled with olive oil and za'atar.
steps: Stir the salt into the yoghurt, then tip it into a muslin-lined sieve set over a bowl.
Chill and let it strain for at least 24 hours until thick and spreadable.
Spread the labneh onto a plate, making a shallow well in the centre.
Sprinkle generously with za'atar and finish with a good pour of olive oil.

name: Kibbeh (Stuffed Bulgur & Meat Croquettes)
description: Torpedo-shaped bulgur shells filled with spiced minced lamb and fried until crisp.
steps: Soak the bulgur in water for 15 minutes, drain well, then blend with half the mince and one grated onion into a smooth, pliable shell paste; chill.
For the filling, brown the remaining mince with the second onion, pine nuts, allspice, and cinnamon.
Wet your hands and shape the shell paste into small torpedoes, hollowing each with your finger and stuffing with the filling before sealing.
Deep-fry in hot sunflower oil for 4–5 minutes until deep brown and crisp, then drain and serve.

name: Moroccan Carrot & Orange Salad
description: A refreshing salad of grated carrot, orange, and orange blossom water spiced with cinnamon.
steps: Coarsely grate the carrots into a bowl.
Segment the oranges over the bowl to catch the juice, then add the segments to the carrot.
Whisk the orange blossom water, cinnamon, olive oil, and honey together and pour over the salad.
Toss well and chill for at least 20 minutes before serving.

name: Pan con Tomate
description: Toasted rustic bread rubbed with garlic and ripe tomato, finished with good olive oil.
steps: Toast or grill the bread slices until golden and lightly crisp.
Halve the garlic cloves and rub the cut side over each warm slice.
Halve the tomatoes and rub the cut side firmly over the bread so the pulp soaks in, discarding the skins.
Drizzle generously with olive oil and season with salt before serving.

name: Yorkshire Pudding
description: Our most popular recipe — light, puffed-up batter pudding, the classic partner to a Sunday roast.
steps: Whisk the flour, eggs, milk, and salt together into a smooth batter and rest for at least 30 minutes.
Pour a little sunflower oil into each hole of a muffin or Yorkshire pudding tin and heat in a 220°C oven until smoking hot.
Carefully pour the batter into the hot tin, filling each hole about halfway.
Bake for 20–25 minutes without opening the oven door, until well risen and deep golden.

name: Fish and Chips
description: Beer-battered fried fish with crisp chunky chips, a British takeaway favourite.
steps: Cut the potatoes into thick chips and fry in batches at a lower temperature (about 140°C) until soft but not coloured; drain.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, salt, and sparkling water into a light, thick batter.
Heat the oil to 190°C, dip the fish fillets in the batter, and fry for 6–8 minutes until golden and crisp.
Return the chips to the hot oil for a final fry until golden, then drain, salt everything well, and serve together.

name: Shepherd's Pie
description: A comforting bake of spiced minced lamb topped with buttery mashed potato.
steps: Boil the potatoes until tender, then mash with the butter and milk; season well.
Brown the lamb mince with the diced onion and carrot.
Stir in the tomato paste, worcestershire sauce, and beef stock, then simmer for 15 minutes until thickened.
Spoon the mince into a baking dish, top with the mashed potato, and bake at 200°C for 20 minutes until golden on top.

name: Full English Breakfast
description: A hearty cooked breakfast plate with eggs, sausages, bacon, beans, and grilled tomato.
steps: Grill or fry the sausages and bacon until cooked through and browned.
Halve the tomatoes and fry the mushrooms in butter alongside them.
Warm the baked beans in a small pan, and fry or poach the eggs to your liking.
Toast the bread and arrange everything together on warm plates to serve.

name: Bangers and Mash
description: Pan-fried sausages served over creamy mashed potato with rich onion gravy.
steps: Fry the sausages gently until browned and cooked through, then set aside.
Boil the potatoes until tender and mash with the butter and milk.
In the same pan, soften the sliced onions, stir in the flour, then gradually add the beef stock to make a rich gravy.
Pile the mash onto plates, top with the sausages, and spoon over the onion gravy.

name: Victoria Sponge Cake
description: A classic British sponge cake sandwiched with strawberry jam and whipped cream.
steps: Cream the butter and caster sugar together until pale and fluffy.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then fold in the self-raising flour.
Divide the batter between two greased 20cm cake tins and bake at 180°C for 20–25 minutes until springy to the touch.
Once cool, sandwich the two sponges together with the jam and whipped double cream.

name: Sticky Toffee Pudding
description: A rich date sponge pudding drenched in warm toffee sauce.
steps: Simmer the dates in water until soft, then blend into a purée.
Cream the butter with half the sugar, beat in the eggs, then fold in the flour and date purée.
Pour into a greased baking dish and bake at 180°C for 25–30 minutes until risen and set.
For the sauce, gently melt the remaining sugar, double cream, and golden syrup together, then pour warm over the pudding.

name: Sunday Roast Beef with Gravy
description: A traditional slow-roasted beef joint with rich pan gravy — the centrepiece of a British Sunday lunch.
steps: Rub the beef joint with olive oil, salt, and pepper, and sit it on a bed of carrots, onions, garlic, and rosemary in a roasting tin.
Roast at 220°C for 20 minutes, then reduce to 180°C and continue roasting until cooked to your liking, about 60–70 minutes more.
Rest the beef, loosely covered, for 20 minutes before carving.
Skim the fat from the roasting tin, stir in the flour, then whisk in the beef stock over heat until you have a smooth gravy.

name: Perfect Fluffy Rice with Vermicelli (Şehriyeli Pirinç)
description: The ultimate Mediterranean side dish — fluffy rice toasted with vermicelli and butter.
steps: Rinse the rice in cold water until it runs clear, then drain well.
Melt the butter in a heavy pan and toast the vermicelli until golden brown.
Add the rice and stir for a minute to coat it in the butter, then pour in the water and salt.
Bring to the boil, cover, and simmer on low heat for 15–18 minutes until the water is absorbed, then rest off the heat for 10 minutes before fluffing with a fork.

name: Kavurma with Eggs (Turkish Sunday Breakfast)
description: A traditional 10-minute Turkish Sunday breakfast of cured beef kavurma fried with eggs.
steps: Melt the butter in a pan over medium heat and add the kavurma.
Fry gently for 2–3 minutes until the beef releases its fat and turns lightly crisp at the edges.
Crack the eggs directly over the kavurma and cook until the whites are just set.
Sprinkle with chilli flakes and serve straight from the pan with fresh bread.

name: Sucuk Spiced Menemen
description: A bold twist on Turkey's beloved breakfast of eggs, tomatoes, and peppers, spiced up with sucuk.
steps: Fry the sliced sucuk in olive oil for 2 minutes until it releases its rich red oil.
Add the diced green pepper and cook until softened.
Stir in the grated tomato and simmer for 5–6 minutes until reduced.
Crack in the eggs and stir gently until softly set, then season with salt and chilli flakes and serve hot with bread.

name: Roasted Pepper Yoghurt Dip
description: A velvety, healthy Mediterranean dip of smoky roasted peppers folded through thick yoghurt.
steps: Roast the red peppers under a hot grill, turning occasionally, until the skins are blackened and blistered.
Wrap in cling film to cool, then peel, deseed, and finely chop the flesh.
Crush the garlic and fold it through the yoghurt with the chopped roasted pepper.
Spoon into a bowl, top with toasted walnuts, a drizzle of olive oil, and a pinch of chilli flakes.

name: Turkish White Bean Stew with Sucuk (Kuru Fasulye)
description: A hearty, slow-simmered Turkish staple of white beans and sucuk in a rich tomato sauce.
steps: Soak the dried beans overnight in plenty of water, then drain.
Sauté the diced onion in olive oil until soft, then add the sliced sucuk and cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, red pepper paste, and paprika.
Add the beans and beef stock, cover, and simmer for 40–45 minutes until the beans are tender, then season and serve with rice.

name: Mediterranean Spiced Lamb Stew
description: A warm, bold lamb stew simmered slowly with Mediterranean spices until meltingly tender.
steps: Brown the diced lamb in olive oil in batches, then set aside.
Soften the onion and garlic in the same pot, then stir in the cumin, paprika, cinnamon, and tomato paste.
Return the lamb to the pot with the carrot and beef stock.
Cover and simmer gently for about an hour until the lamb is fork-tender, then season and serve with rice or bread.

name: Weeknight Chickpea Stew
description: A quick, comforting chickpea stew in a rich tomato sauce with warming Mediterranean spices.
steps: Sauté the diced onion and garlic in olive oil until softened.
Stir in the tomato paste, cumin, and paprika and cook for a minute until fragrant.
Add the chickpeas and vegetable stock and bring to a simmer.
Cook for 20–25 minutes until thickened, then season and serve with rice or crusty bread.

name: Aşure (Noah's Pudding)
description: A traditional Turkish dessert of grains, pulses, and dried fruit, symbolising abundance and sharing.
steps: Soak the wheat berries, chickpeas, and white beans separately in water overnight.
Cook the wheat berries in fresh water for about 45 minutes until tender, then add the cooked chickpeas and beans.
Stir in the dried apricot, fig, raisins, sugar, and orange zest, and simmer for 20 minutes until thickened to a soft porridge.
Chill and serve garnished with walnuts and a light dusting of cinnamon.

name: Viral Turkish Yoghurt Cake
description: A wobbly, cloud-like Turkish yoghurt cake that has taken social media by storm.
steps: Whisk the eggs and sugar together until pale, thick, and fluffy.
Fold in the yoghurt and vanilla extract until smooth.
Gently fold in the flour and baking powder, taking care not to knock out the air.
Pour into a lined tin and bake at 170°C for 25–30 minutes until golden and springy, then cool before slicing.

name: Bodrum Sour Cherry Jam Cheesecake
description: A creamy, no-bake vanilla cheesecake crowned with sweet-tart sour cherry jam.
steps: Crush the digestive biscuits and mix with the melted butter, then press firmly into the base of a lined tin and chill.
Whisk the cream cheese, double cream, sugar, and vanilla together until thick and holding soft peaks.
Spread the filling evenly over the chilled biscuit base.
Top with the sour cherry jam and chill for at least 4 hours, or overnight, before serving.

name: Dubai-Inspired Chocolate Bar
description: The viral pistachio and kadayif chocolate bar, made at home with crunchy shredded phyllo.
steps: Chop the kadayif into short strands and toast in the butter until golden and crisp; leave to cool.
Mix the toasted kadayif with the pistachio paste and tahini to make the filling.
Melt half the chocolate and coat the base and sides of bar moulds, then chill briefly to set.
Fill with the pistachio-kadayif mixture, seal with the remaining melted chocolate, scatter with chopped pistachios, and chill until firm.

name: Mediterranean Chicken Marinade
description: Grilled chicken marinated in red wine vinegar, olive oil, garlic, and oregano.
steps: Whisk together the red wine vinegar, olive oil, crushed garlic, oregano, lemon juice, and salt.
Coat the chicken thoroughly in the marinade and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or overnight for best flavour.
Grill or pan-fry the chicken over high heat until charred and cooked through, about 8–10 minutes per side.
Rest for 5 minutes before slicing and serving.

name: Creamy Mediterranean Chicken Orzo
description: A one-pot, quick gourmet meal of orzo pasta, chicken, and mushrooms in a creamy sauce.
steps: Sear the diced chicken in olive oil until golden, then set aside.
In the same pan, sauté the sliced mushrooms and garlic until softened.
Stir in the orzo and toast briefly, then ladle in the stock gradually, stirring often, for about 15 minutes until the orzo is tender.
Return the chicken to the pan, stir through the cream and parmesan, and season before serving.

name: Spaghetti Bolognese
description: A deep, slow-cooked ragù alla Bolognese, the ultimate authentic Italian classic.
steps: Finely dice the onion, carrot, and celery, and soften in olive oil with the garlic.
Add the mince and brown well, breaking it up as it cooks.
Stir in the tomato paste, then the chopped tomatoes, and simmer gently for 45 minutes, stirring occasionally, until rich and thick.
Cook the spaghetti until al dente and serve topped with the ragù and grated parmesan.

name: Olive & Sun-Dried Tomato Mezze Platter
description: A shareable Mediterranean mezze spread built around olives, sun-dried tomatoes, and feta.
steps: Arrange the olives, sun-dried tomatoes, and cubed feta across a large sharing platter.
Spoon a generous bowl of hummus into the centre.
Warm the flatbread and cut into wedges to serve alongside.
Finish with a good drizzle of olive oil and a scatter of dried oregano.

name: Chilli Con Carne
description: A deep, smoky, award-worthy chilli — a British takeaway and dinner-table favourite.
steps: Brown the mince with the diced onion and garlic in a large pot.
Stir in the smoked paprika, cumin, and chilli flakes and cook for a minute until fragrant.
Add the tomato paste, chopped tomatoes, beef stock, and kidney beans.
Simmer uncovered for 45–50 minutes, stirring occasionally, until rich and thick, then season and serve with rice or crusty bread.

name: Homemade Apple Crumble
description: A warm, comforting British dessert of tender spiced apples under a crisp buttery topping.
steps: Peel, core, and slice the apples into a baking dish, tossing with a little sugar and cinnamon.
Rub the flour and butter together until it resembles coarse breadcrumbs, then stir in the remaining sugar and oats.
Scatter the crumble topping evenly over the apples.
Bake at 190°C for 35–40 minutes until golden and bubbling, and serve warm with custard or cream.

name: Fluffy Homemade Pancakes
description: A stack of warm, fluffy pancakes with a cosy touch of cinnamon — a weekend breakfast favourite.
steps: Whisk the flour, baking powder, sugar, and cinnamon together in a bowl.
Whisk in the eggs and milk until you have a smooth, thick batter.
Melt a little butter in a non-stick pan and ladle in portions of the batter.
Cook for 2–3 minutes per side until golden and cooked through, then stack and serve warm.

name: Domates Pilavı (Turkish Tomato Rice Pilaf)
description: A simple, everyday Turkish rice pilaf cooked with tomato paste and butter until fluffy.
steps: Rinse the rice in cold water until it runs clear, then drain well.
Melt the butter in a pan and stir in the tomato paste, cooking for a minute until fragrant.
Add the rice and stir to coat, then pour in the stock and salt and bring to the boil.
Cover and simmer for 15 minutes, then rest off the heat for 10 minutes before fluffing with a fork.

name: İç Pilav (Ottoman Rice Pilaf with Currants & Pine Nuts)
description: A fragrant Ottoman-era rice pilaf studded with currants, pine nuts, and warm spices.
steps: Soak the currants in warm water for 10 minutes, then drain.
Sauté the diced onion in olive oil until soft, add the pine nuts, and toast until golden.
Stir in the rice, allspice, and cinnamon, coating well, then add the stock and currants.
Bring to the boil, cover, simmer for 15 minutes, rest for 10 minutes, then fold through the chopped dill before serving.

name: Nohutlu Pilav (Chickpea Rice Pilaf)
description: A hearty one-pot Turkish rice and chickpea pilaf, a comforting weeknight staple.
steps: Sauté the diced onion in olive oil until soft, then stir in the tomato paste and paprika.
Add the rice and chickpeas, stirring to coat in the paste.
Pour in the stock and salt and bring to the boil.
Cover, simmer for 15 minutes, then rest off the heat for 10 minutes before fluffing.

name: Kuzu Etli Pilav (Lamb Rice Pilaf)
description: Tender braised lamb folded through buttery, fragrant rice pilaf.
steps: Brown the diced lamb in butter, then add the onion and soften.
Stir in the allspice and cinnamon, pour in half the stock, cover, and simmer for 40 minutes until the lamb is tender.
Stir in the rinsed rice and the remaining stock, and season with salt.
Cover, simmer for 15 minutes, then rest for 10 minutes off the heat before fluffing.

name: Spanakorizo (Greek Spinach Rice)
description: A bright, lemony Greek rice dish loaded with spinach and fresh dill.
steps: Soften the diced onion in olive oil, then add the rice and stir for a minute.
Add the stock and salt, bring to a simmer, and cook for 10 minutes.
Stir in the spinach and cook until wilted and the rice is tender, about 8 minutes more.
Off the heat, stir through the chopped dill and a good squeeze of lemon juice.

name: Biber Dolması (Rice-Stuffed Peppers)
description: Green peppers stuffed with spiced rice, tomato, and herbs, gently simmered in olive oil.
steps: Slice the tops off the peppers and hollow out the seeds.
Mix the rice with diced onion, grated tomato, tomato paste, olive oil, dried mint, and chopped parsley for the filling.
Spoon the filling into the peppers, leaving room for the rice to expand, and arrange upright in a pot.
Add the water, cover, and simmer for 40–45 minutes until the peppers are tender and the rice is cooked through.

name: Sütlaç (Turkish Rice Pudding)
description: A creamy baked Turkish rice pudding with a golden top — a classic milk-based dessert.
steps: Simmer the rice in a little water until softened, then drain.
Add the milk and sugar, and cook gently for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Whisk the cornflour with a splash of cold milk, stir into the pot, and cook until thickened.
Off the heat, stir in the vanilla and egg yolks, pour into ramekins, and grill until golden on top; chill before serving.

name: Bulgur Pilavı (Turkish Bulgur Pilaf)
description: A simple, everyday Turkish bulgur pilaf with tomato and green pepper — the classic partner to grilled meats.
steps: Sauté the diced pepper in olive oil until softened, then stir in the tomato paste.
Add the diced tomato and cook for a few minutes until it breaks down.
Stir in the bulgur, then pour in the stock and salt.
Bring to the boil, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, then rest for 10 minutes before fluffing.

name: Mercimekli Bulgur Pilavı (Bulgur Pilaf with Red Lentils)
description: A rustic, protein-rich bulgur and red lentil pilaf, warmed with cumin and paprika.
steps: Sauté the onion in olive oil until golden, then stir in the cumin and paprika.
Add the red lentils and stock, bring to a simmer, and cook for 10 minutes until the lentils soften.
Stir in the bulgur and salt, cover, and simmer for 12–15 minutes until all the liquid is absorbed.
Rest for 5 minutes off the heat before serving.

name: Mercimekli Köfte (Lentil & Bulgur Patties)
description: No-cook-required vegan bulgur and red lentil patties, packed with herbs and spice.
steps: Cook the red lentils in water until soft, about 15 minutes, then drain any excess liquid.
While still hot, stir in the bulgur and cover for 10 minutes so it steams and softens.
Sauté the onion in olive oil until deep golden, then stir in the tomato paste, cumin, and chilli flakes.
Mix everything together with the chopped spring onion and parsley, shape into small ovals, and serve with lemon wedges.

name: Mujaddara (Bulgur with Lentils & Caramelised Onions)
description: A humble, deeply comforting Levantine classic of bulgur and lentils topped with sweet caramelised onions.
steps: Cook the lentils in the stock for 15–20 minutes until just tender.
Meanwhile, thinly slice the onions and fry slowly in olive oil for 20 minutes until deep golden and caramelised.
Stir the bulgur and cumin into the lentils, cover, and simmer for 12–15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed.
Season with salt, pile onto a plate, and top generously with the caramelised onions.
